payload.headline: Tesla jumps 11.46% to 385.46 without business news; margins and cash still shrinking, avoid

summary.thesis: The price rebounded sharply, but the business beneath it is the same: flat sales, thinner margins and half the free cash flow, priced near the top of its own history.
summary.decision: Long-term avoid (unchanged); swing wait, because the price sits just under a heavy resistance zone with no clean trend.
summary.act_at: Re-examine long-term at 293.94; swing only on a close above 404.4 or a hold at 363.89–368.73

payload.happening: Tesla rose 11.46% to 385.46. That undoes the last session's fall to 345.82 and puts the price back above its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages (384.49, 376.17, 381.53), all of them flat. The only news was two reports: The Verge described new visuals in the FSD v15 driver-assist software (preliminary), and the Financial Times reported that Mercedes has an edge over Tesla in self-driving in Europe. Neither explains the jump in business terms. The next earnings report is due 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Nothing in today's data changes the business. The latest filing (quarter ending 2026-09-30, filed 2026-10-22) still shows sales flat: -0.17% versus a year earlier, after 15.78% two quarters before. Operating margin, the share of sales left after running costs, fell to 3.35% from 4.74%. Trailing free cash flow (cash left after investment) fell to 3.3B from 6.8B. Inventory is up 15% while sales are up 0%. Unsold cars can lead to price cuts and lower margins. Returns on new spending have dropped to 5¢ per dollar from 33¢ three years ago. At risk: margins and cash generation, if demand stays flat. Not at risk: the balance sheet. Net cash is 37.5B and total liquidity is 45.4B against 8.0B of debt, so there is no funding problem. The Mercedes report is about competition in self-driving. For now it affects sentiment, not sales or margins in the filings. The FSD v15 report only touches how the product is perceived. Neither news item raises a governance issue.

worth.text: At 385.46, Tesla is worth 1524.0B. That is 424.1 times trailing earnings and 14.7 times sales. A discounted-cash-flow model (today's value of future cash) starts from the 3.3B of free cash flow and a 10.0% discount rate. It gives 20.01 (bear), 24.66 (base) and 44.3 (bull) per share. Even with sales growth starting at 30% a year, it reaches only 44.63. The filings note that the price needs about 51% a year growth against 3% a year delivered over three years. The second method uses Tesla's own 5-year price-to-sales history and gives 203.8 (low), 293.94 (middle) and 399.81 (high). The price is close to that high end, and price-to-sales sits at the 63rd percentile of its own 5-year range. The whole gap between the two methods comes from one assumption: whether investors keep paying a high multiple of sales whatever the cash flow, or value the stock on the cash it actually produces. Stalled growth argues for the low-to-middle part of the own-history range.
worth.key_assumption: The market keeps valuing Tesla on its own 5-year price-to-sales history at the low-to-middle level that flat sales justify, not near the 399.81 top and not on its 3.3B of free cash flow.

bull: Net cash of 37.5B and liquidity of 45.4B give Tesla years of room to fund new projects without borrowing.
Sales grew 15.78% only two quarters ago, so the flat -0.17% quarter could prove to be a pause rather than a trend.
The price closed at 385.46, back above the 50-day (376.17) and 200-day (381.53) averages, and the busiest call strike for 2026-12-18 is 400 with 14601 contracts open.
bear: Trailing free cash flow halved to 3.3B from 6.8B, while the market value is 1524.0B.
Operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%, and inventory is up 15% on sales up 0%, which points to possible price cuts.
The DCF base value is 24.66 per share, and even the own-history middle of 293.94 sits below today's 385.46.

levels.what: Today's close. It is near the own-history high of 399.81 and far above the DCF base of 24.66, so the jump made the stock more expensive, not cheaper.
Bottom of the nearest support zone (363.89–368.73), touched 4 times. A close below it would end the rebound.
Middle of the own-history price-to-sales range. Re-examine here only if the 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 3.35%.

longterm.why: Sales have stalled, margins and free cash flow are shrinking, and the price sits near the top of its own valuation history. The business is graded D, and the committee call is Reduce.

swing.why: The price sits in the 380.15–389.95 zone, just below resistance at 393.63–404.4 (touched 5 times), and the overall trend is still marked downtrend. Room to the first resistance is less than one ATR of 19.35, so the setup is poor. No trade until a close above 404.4 or a pullback that holds 363.89–368.73.

decision.timing: No new long-term position before the 2027-01-27 report, the next test of margins, inventory and cash. The options moves (14.2% by 2026-12-18, 22.1% by 2027-02-19) were priced on 2026-11-20 at 345.82, before today's jump, so they understate the current range.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly sales growth back above 0%. That would move the long-term view off avoid, toward buying near 293.94.
Trailing free cash flow recovers toward the prior 6.8B, which would lift the DCF values and narrow the gap to the price.
Swing: a close above 404.4 (top of the 393.63–404.4 resistance) would open a move toward 408.62–417.44. A close below 363.89 would confirm the downtrend and return the swing call to no trade.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid. The 11.46% jump to 385.46 changed the price, not the business, where trailing free cash flow is still 3.3B against 6.8B a year earlier. The swing call moved from no trade to wait, because the price is back above its averages but just under resistance.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
